investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the candidate's own official domain (divandumonde.com) and its /fr, /en subpaths, plus a follow-up probe of the domain that site's own 'RÉSERVATION' button links to. This settled a genuine identity question at Level 1 — no escalation was needed or would have helped.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.divandumonde.com/ returned a page carrying essentially zero real content beyond a page title ('Divan du monde - Madame Arthur'), a logo, and a stale '© 2023 Divan du monde - Madame Arthur' footer notice — no events, agenda, or programme content of any kind. The page's own single 'RÉSERVATION' button links out to https://club.madamearthur.fr/, a domain that does not resolve at all (DNS failure). The site's own /en subpath separately failed (an HTTP 500 on one attempt, a connection timeout on a second attempt minutes later) and /fr silently redirects back to the same near-empty home page. This fully and sufficiently answered the investigation question at Level 1: divandumonde.com is a stale, effectively abandoned placeholder with no first-party event data and a broken outbound link — no amount of further static or structural probing of THIS domain would change that finding, so no escalation was attempted.

identity.notes: divandumonde.com IS this project's assigned candidate's own registered domain (its JSON-LD Organization block directly states 'name':'Divan du Monde', logo, and Facebook/Instagram 'sameAs' links matching the venue), but it carries no active first-party event content — a stale placeholder, not a maintained official presence. The physical location's actual currently-operating brand is a SEPARATE, distinct first-party site: madamearthur.fr ('Madame Arthur - Cabaret Club'), whose own retained 'notre histoire' text directly states: 'En 2015, Madame Arthur et le Divan fusionnent pour créer le Cabaret-Club que l'on connait aujourd'hui' ('In 2015, Madame Arthur and the Divan merged to create the Cabaret-Club we know today'). This is a genuine identity-merger finding, not an assumption: the assigned candidate 'Le Divan du Monde', as an independent brand/identity with its own maintained official presence, does not currently exist. Continuing this investigation under the 'Le Divan du Monde' identity, or silently substituting 'Madame Arthur' as if it were the same assigned candidate, would both misrepresent what was actually found.

reasons: divandumonde.com — this candidate's own official domain — carries no maintained first-party event content: a stale '© 2023' placeholder page with no agenda, programme, or events listing of any kind.

The page's own single call-to-action ('RÉSERVATION') links to https://club.madamearthur.fr/, which does not resolve at all (DNS failure) — a broken link on the candidate's own official page, not merely an inconvenient one.

The candidate's own '/en' subpath independently failed on two separate attempts (an HTTP 500, then a connection timeout minutes later) and '/fr' silently redirects back to the same near-empty home page.

This project's own retained evidence (madamearthur.fr's own 'notre histoire' text) directly states that 'Le Divan du Monde' merged into a different, separately-branded entity ('Madame Arthur') in 2015 — the assigned candidate, as an independent identity, genuinely no longer maintains its own official presence.

Per policy, an investigation must not invent or silently substitute a venue identity: continuing under 'Le Divan du Monde' as if it still had a live official site, or quietly investigating 'Madame Arthur' instead as though it were the same assignment, would both misrepresent what was actually found. REJECT is the honest outcome for the assigned candidate as such; a future, separately-scoped investigation of 'Madame Arthur' (its own distinct identity, primarily a cabaret/drag/DJ-club format rather than a live-music concert hall) would need its own investigation_id if this project wants coverage of the physical venue at this address.
No fabricated fact was used to reach this decision — every claim above is cited to retained evidence.
